source.title: Improving Layer-wise Adaptive Rate Methods using Trust Ratio Clipping
source.authors: Jeffrey Fong; Si-Wei Chen; Kaiqi Chen

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether trust-ratio clipping changes test performance, using a LAMB variant rather than the original claim’s interventions. It does not directly test any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-accuracy comparisons for clipping versus no clipping and for several clipping bounds. Those results concern generalization but do not test a listed version. The cited prior-work results in the introduction and references are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Table 1 tests V5 in a new optimizer setting: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 with learning rate 0.01 and 80 epochs held fixed across batches of 1000, 2000, and 3000. These cross-batch results bear on V5 even though the authors emphasize clipping versus no clipping.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: LAMBC outperforms LAMB in their reported CIFAR-10 and downsampled ImageNet experiments, and clipping-bound selection matters. Their broader statement about effectiveness across small and large batches exceeds the demonstrated batch-size coverage.
record.recipe_differences: Adds trust-ratio clipping to LAMB and compares against unclipped LAMB; this is not the original claim’s memorization, architecture, optimizer, regularization, sharpness, or example-removal method.
record.method_sensitivity: CIFAR-10 test performance varied with clipping upper bound; the paper reports bound 1 best and 10 worst. It also reports results at batch sizes 1000, 2000, and 3000, with differing accuracies.

fits_no_version.finding: Trust-ratio clipping improves test accuracy over unclipped LAMB at each tested batch size, and its upper bound affects performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trust-ratio clipping can improve LAMB test accuracy in the reported CIFAR-10 and downsampled ImageNet settings.

record.problems: The paper says it could not test larger batch sizes (> 8K on CIFAR-10 and > 1K on ImageNet). ImageNet results are figure-only, with no numerical values in the text. The paper notes that the ImageNet model appears to overfit the training data. No uncertainty estimates are stated.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out performance.
Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under specified tuning budgets.

Conventional small-batch baselines, the workload-dependent threshold, longer training, learning-rate scaling or warmup, normalization or regularization adaptations, and language models. Clipping improves accuracy at each tested batch size, but recovery to a small-batch baseline is not established.
Dropout interventions and their interactions with dataset size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to train-test gaps.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal and subsequent retraining.

missing.what: Fixed-epoch batch-size comparisons within LAMBC: increasing batch size from 1000 to 2000 lowers accuracy by 0.41 percentage points; increasing it to 3000 lowers accuracy by 1.42 points relative to 1000.

Fixed-epoch batch-size comparisons within LAMB: batch 2000 improves accuracy by 0.93 percentage points over 1000, while batch 3000 lowers accuracy by 0.27 points relative to 1000 and 1.20 points relative to 2000.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly dismisses V5: its own extracted table contains a fixed-epoch batch-size sweep. The nonmonotonic unclipped result does not challenge V5, which allows a workload-dependent threshold. No uncertainty estimates establish whether the smaller accuracy differences are reliable.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison with natural-label generalization.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
Batch sizes vary, but the paper does not compare large and small batches under the version’s fixed-epoch setup or test the claimed large-batch penalty.
No sharpness or other measured property is related to the train-test gap.
No memorized-example removal or retraining comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with LAMBC trust-ratio clipping; compared with LAMB without clipping.
rows.note: Authors describe the improvement at batch size 1K as about 2%.
rows.check: The accuracies provide the batch-1000 reference for V5, but the recorded baseline compares optimizers at the same batch size. That contrast alone cannot establish a batch-size effect. Clipping is a training-optimizer intervention, not a post-training weight edit.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with LAMBC trust-ratio clipping; compared with LAMB without clipping.
rows.note: Authors describe the improvement at batch size 2K as about 0.7%.
rows.check: The recorded contrast measures clipping, not increasing batch size. Relative to batch 1000, batch 2000 lowers clipped accuracy by 0.41 percentage points but raises unclipped accuracy by 0.93 points; separate batch-comparison rows are needed.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with LAMBC trust-ratio clipping; compared with LAMB without clipping.
rows.note: Authors describe the improvement at batch size 3K as about 0.7%.
rows.check: The recorded baseline compares clipping conditions. For V5, batch 3000 should instead be compared with smaller batches within each optimizer: accuracy falls under both clipping conditions. The clipping gain itself is 0.88 percentage points, rather than approximately 0.7.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy across trust-ratio clipping upper bounds; no-clipping setup is the reference.
rows.note: The text says all clipped conditions outperform no clipping, and describes bound 1 as best, 10 as worst, with 3 and 5 in between.
rows.check: This clipping-bound comparison reports the proposed method's performance and does not measure any listed version. Its observed state cannot be transferred to a claim version.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared ImageNet test performance with and without trust-ratio clipping.
rows.note: The text says clipping helps generalization performance and outperforms the model without clipping; model name and numerical values are not stated.
rows.check: The ImageNet experiment compares clipping conditions at one batch size, with no SGD comparator or other listed intervention. Its qualitative improvement does not establish any listed version.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 ResNet-18, 80 epochs, learning rate 0.01, LAMBC with clipping bound 1; batches 1000–3000.
relationships.reason: Table 1 shows accuracy decreasing from 87.71% to 87.30% to 86.29% as batch size increases. Based on the text and cross-batch values in R1–R3; the missing batch-comparison rows should record this contrast.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy decreased as batches increased with clipping, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Same CIFAR-10 recipe with unclipped LAMB; batch 3000 versus batches 1000 and 2000.
relationships.reason: Table 1 gives 85.41% at batch 3000 versus 85.68% at 1000 and 86.61% at 2000. Based on cross-batch values in R1–R3; the intermediate improvement means the trend is not monotonic.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy was lower at the largest batch after improving at intermediate batch sizes, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
